edits.text: 1. PURCHASE PRICE. The Buyer shall pay the Seller the purchase price for the Shares (the “Purchase Price”), in an amount to be agreed in writing by the parties. The Purchase Price shall be subject to adjustment for any indebtedness, transaction expenses, and working-capital shortfall of the Seller as of Closing, in each case as determined in accordance with the principles and procedures to be set forth in a mutually agreed closing statement. The Buyer may offset any amounts then due from the Seller under this Agreement against amounts payable to the Seller. The parties shall cooperate in good faith to prepare and resolve the closing statement promptly following Closing.

2. CLOSING. Closing shall occur within thirty days after signing, or on such other date as the parties agree in writing, subject to satisfaction or waiver by the Buyer of the conditions to Closing set forth in this Agreement. The Buyer’s obligation to close is conditioned on the Seller’s representations and warranties being true and correct in all material respects as of Closing, the Seller having performed in all material respects its obligations due at or before Closing, and no order or legal restraint prohibiting the transaction being in effect. At Closing, the Seller shall deliver the Shares free and clear of all liens and the customary transfer instruments and other documents reasonably required to consummate the transaction.

3. REPRESENTATIONS. The Seller represents and warrants to the Buyer, as of signing and as of Closing, that: (a) the financial statements delivered to the Buyer have been prepared consistently with the Seller’s past practices and fairly present, in all material respects, the Seller’s financial condition and results of operations for the periods covered; (b) the Seller has no liabilities other than liabilities reflected or reserved against in those financial statements or incurred in the ordinary course since their date; and (c) the Seller has authority to enter into and perform this Agreement and transfer the Shares. The Seller shall promptly disclose to the Buyer any fact or circumstance arising before Closing that would make any representation or warranty inaccurate in any material respect.

4. INDEMNITY. The Seller shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the Buyer and its affiliates and their respective representatives from and against all losses, liabilities, damages, costs, and expenses (including reasonable legal fees) arising out of or relating to (a) any breach of a representation, warranty, covenant, or agreement of the Seller under this Agreement, or (b) any liability of the Seller not expressly assumed by the Buyer. The Buyer may recover covered amounts by setoff against any amounts payable to the Seller. The procedures, survival periods, and any limitations applicable to indemnification shall be set forth in this Agreement and shall not limit recovery for fraud or intentional misrepresentation.

receiver.message_back: We cannot accept the purchase-price adjustment or indemnity as drafted: the adjustment lacks agreed accounting rules, a dispute process, and limits on Buyer’s unilateral setoff, while the indemnity is uncapped and covers broadly defined unassumed liabilities. Please provide a complete draft with agreed adjustment mechanics and a balanced, capped indemnity (including customary baskets, survival periods, and exclusive-remedy provisions), together with reciprocal Buyer representations and appropriately limited closing conditions.

drafter.private_reasoning: The draft should address the stated objections without disclosing the client’s confidential authorization. I have supplied operational purchase-price mechanics, a neutral accounting dispute process, restricted setoff, mutual representations and conditions, and a capped, time-limited indemnity with customary exceptions.
drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel: Attached are our proposed revisions for a complete adjustment and indemnity framework. The revisions add agreed accounting conventions, an estimate-and-true-up process with independent-accountant resolution, and limit setoff to amounts agreed or finally determined. They also provide reciprocal representations and closing conditions, and replace the broad uncapped indemnity with a mutual, basket- and cap-based exclusive remedy, subject to customary exceptions. The purchase price remains to be completed in the parties’ written purchase-price schedule.

edits.text:
1. PURCHASE PRICE; ADJUSTMENT.
(a) Purchase Price. The aggregate purchase price for the Shares (the “Purchase Price”) shall be the amount set forth in a purchase-price schedule signed by both parties before Closing. The Purchase Price shall be adjusted dollar-for-dollar by (i) plus or minus the amount by which Closing Working Capital is greater or less than the Target Working Capital, respectively, (ii) minus Closing Indebtedness, and (iii) minus Seller Transaction Expenses, in each case without duplication. “Closing Working Capital” means the current assets of the Seller included in the line items identified in the agreed illustrative calculation, less the current liabilities included in those line items, and excludes cash, Indebtedness, Seller Transaction Expenses, income-tax assets and liabilities, and deferred-tax assets and liabilities. “Target Working Capital” shall be set forth in that schedule. “Indebtedness” and “Seller Transaction Expenses” shall be defined in the schedule; Seller Transaction Expenses include unpaid transaction-related fees and expenses payable by or on behalf of Seller. The schedule shall include an illustrative calculation of Closing Working Capital and the adjustment items.
(b) Accounting rules. The closing statement and all calculations under this Section shall be prepared in accordance with the specific accounting principles, policies, practices, classifications, judgments, and estimation methodologies used in the illustrative calculation, applied consistently with the Seller’s past practice, and, to the extent not addressed thereby, in accordance with GAAP as in effect on the date of this Agreement. The foregoing hierarchy shall control in the event of conflict. No change in accounting method, policy, practice, or classification shall be made solely as a result of the transaction.
(c) Estimated closing payment and statement. At least three Business Days before Closing, Seller shall deliver a good-faith estimate of Closing Working Capital, Closing Indebtedness, and Seller Transaction Expenses, with reasonable supporting detail. At Closing, Buyer shall pay the Purchase Price, adjusted using those estimates, less any amounts paid at Closing on Seller’s behalf under the agreed schedule. Within 60 days after Closing, Buyer shall deliver to Seller a proposed closing statement setting forth its calculation of the final adjustment, with reasonable supporting documentation and access to relevant books and personnel. Buyer shall prepare that statement in accordance with this Section and shall not unreasonably delay its delivery. Seller shall have 45 days after receipt to review it and give written notice of any disputed items, with reasonable detail. Any item not timely disputed shall be final and binding. The parties shall negotiate disputed items in good faith for 30 days.
(d) Expert determination. Any items remaining disputed shall be submitted to an independent nationally recognized accounting firm mutually selected by the parties (the “Accounting Firm”), acting as an expert and not an arbitrator. The Accounting Firm shall consider only the disputed items, shall apply this Section, shall not assign a value to any item greater than the highest value proposed by either party or less than the lowest value proposed by either party, and shall issue a reasoned written determination within 30 days, or as promptly as practicable. Each party shall provide submissions to the other simultaneously and shall have a reasonable opportunity to respond. The determination shall be final and binding absent manifest error. The Accounting Firm’s fees shall be allocated between the parties in inverse proportion to the extent each party’s positions are not sustained. The final closing statement shall be binding and the resulting payment shall be made by wire transfer within five Business Days, together with interest from Closing at the prime rate published by The Wall Street Journal. No party may recover twice for the same amount.
(e) Setoff. Neither party may set off or withhold any amount otherwise payable under this Agreement, except for an amount agreed in writing by the other party or finally determined to be due under this Section or a final, non-appealable judgment. This Section is the exclusive procedure for resolving purchase-price adjustment claims.

edits.text:
2. CLOSING; CONDITIONS.
(a) Closing shall occur within 30 days after signing, or on another date agreed in writing, by electronic exchange of deliverables and funds (the “Closing Date”), subject to satisfaction or waiver in writing by the party entitled to the applicable condition. No party may rely on the failure of a condition to the extent caused by its breach of this Agreement.
(b) Conditions to each party’s obligation to close are (i) no law or order of a court of competent jurisdiction in effect that prohibits consummation of the transaction and (ii) all governmental approvals required to consummate the transaction having been obtained and remaining in effect. No condition shall require any party to accept a materially burdensome condition imposed by a governmental authority.
(c) Buyer’s obligation to close is additionally conditioned on Seller’s representations and warranties being true and correct as of signing and Closing, disregarding materiality qualifiers for this purpose, except where the failure to be true and correct would not, individually or in the aggregate, reasonably be expected to have a material adverse effect on Seller; provided that fundamental representations concerning organization, authority, title to Shares, and brokers shall be true in all material respects. Seller shall have performed in all material respects its covenants required to be performed by Closing. Seller shall deliver a certificate confirming satisfaction of these conditions in all material respects.
(d) Seller’s obligation to close is additionally conditioned on Buyer’s representations and warranties being true and correct as of signing and Closing, disregarding materiality qualifiers for this purpose, except where the failure to be true and correct would not reasonably be expected to materially impair Buyer’s ability to consummate the transaction; Buyer shall have performed in all material respects its covenants required to be performed by Closing and shall deliver the Purchase Price payable at Closing. Buyer shall deliver a certificate confirming satisfaction of these conditions in all material respects.
(e) At Closing, Seller shall deliver the Shares, duly endorsed or accompanied by customary transfer instruments, free and clear of liens created by Seller, and the customary closing certificates and instruments. Buyer shall deliver the amount payable at Closing and customary closing certificates and instruments. Each party shall use commercially reasonable efforts to satisfy its respective conditions and cooperate in obtaining required approvals.

edits.text:
3. REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES.
(a) Seller represents and warrants to Buyer as of signing and as of Closing that: (i) Seller is duly organized, validly existing, and has authority to enter into and perform this Agreement; (ii) execution and performance have been duly authorized and do not violate Seller’s organizational documents or any material agreement binding on Seller; (iii) Seller owns the Shares of record and beneficially, free and clear of liens created by Seller, and has authority to transfer them; (iv) the financial statements delivered to Buyer were prepared consistently with Seller’s past practices and fairly present, in all material respects, Seller’s financial condition and results of operations for the periods covered; (v) to Seller’s knowledge, Seller has no liabilities required to be reflected in those financial statements other than liabilities reflected or reserved against therein or incurred in the ordinary course since their date, and no such ordinary-course liabilities are material individually or in the aggregate; and (vi) no broker or finder is entitled to a fee from Buyer based on arrangements made by Seller.
(b) Buyer represents and warrants to Seller as of signing and as of Closing that: (i) Buyer is duly organized, validly existing, and has authority to enter into and perform this Agreement; (ii) execution and performance have been duly authorized and do not violate Buyer’s organizational documents or any material agreement binding on Buyer; (iii) Buyer has, and at Closing will have, funds sufficient to pay the amounts payable by Buyer at Closing and perform its payment obligations under this Agreement; and (iv) no broker or finder is entitled to a fee from Seller based on arrangements made by Buyer.
(c) Each party shall promptly notify the other in writing if it becomes aware before Closing of a fact that would cause a representation or warranty made by it to be materially inaccurate, provided that notice shall not cure a breach or modify the applicable closing conditions or remedies. Each party’s representations and warranties are subject to the express limitations and survival periods in this Agreement.
edits.name: 3. REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES

edits.text:
4. INDEMNIFICATION; EXCLUSIVE REMEDY.
(a) Seller shall indemnify Buyer and its officers, directors, and employees (the “Buyer Indemnified Parties”) against losses actually incurred, to the extent arising from (i) a breach of Seller’s representations and warranties in this Agreement or (ii) a breach by Seller of its covenants in this Agreement. Buyer shall indemnify Seller and its officers, directors, and employees (the “Seller Indemnified Parties”) against losses actually incurred, to the extent arising from (i) a breach of Buyer’s representations and warranties in this Agreement, (ii) a breach by Buyer of its covenants in this Agreement, or (iii) liabilities expressly assumed by Buyer under this Agreement. Neither party shall be liable for consequential, exemplary, punitive, or special damages, or for lost profits, except to the extent actually awarded to a third party in a third-party claim or arising from fraud. “Losses” excludes amounts reserved or accrued in the final closing statement, amounts covered by insurance or third-party recovery (net of recovery costs and premium increases), and amounts otherwise recovered under this Agreement; the indemnified party shall use commercially reasonable efforts to mitigate Losses.
(b) Except for breaches of Fundamental Representations, neither party shall have liability for representation-and-warranty claims unless aggregate covered Losses exceed 1% of the Purchase Price, in which case the responsible party is liable only for Losses in excess of that amount. “Fundamental Representations” means the representations in Sections 3(a)(i)-(iii) and 3(b)(i)-(iii). The aggregate liability of Seller for claims for breach of representations and warranties other than Fundamental Representations shall not exceed 10% of the Purchase Price. Aggregate liability for breaches of Fundamental Representations and covenants shall not exceed the Purchase Price; provided that nothing in this Agreement limits liability for fraud. The basket and caps apply separately to each party’s liability and shall not permit double recovery. The exclusions and caps in this subsection do not limit payment obligations under Section 1 or amounts expressly payable under a covenant, except that covenant claims remain subject to the applicable cap stated above, other than fraud.
(c) Representations and warranties survive Closing for 12 months, except Fundamental Representations, which survive for six years after Closing. Covenants survive in accordance with their terms, and any covenant that by its terms is to be performed after Closing survives until performed, subject to the applicable cap. A claim noticed in reasonable detail before expiration survives until finally resolved. No claim may be brought after the applicable survival period except as so noticed.
(d) An indemnified party shall give prompt written notice of a claim, describing it in reasonable detail; delay relieves the indemnifying party only to the extent materially prejudiced. For a third-party claim, the indemnifying party may assume the defense with counsel reasonably acceptable to the indemnified party, at its expense, by prompt written notice. The indemnified party may participate with its own counsel at its expense. No settlement imposing non-monetary relief or an admission of wrongdoing on an indemnified party, or not providing an unconditional release, may be made without that party’s written consent, not unreasonably withheld. The indemnifying party may not settle without the indemnified party’s consent if it fails to assume or diligently conduct the defense.
(e) Following Closing, indemnification under this Section is the exclusive remedy for any claim arising out of this Agreement or the transaction, except for claims for fraud, claims for specific performance or other equitable relief, and disputes under Section 1, which are governed exclusively by that Section. No party may set off an indemnity claim against any payment due under this Agreement except for an amount agreed in writing or finally determined by a non-appealable judgment. Nothing herein limits a party’s right to seek equitable relief before Closing.
